item.title: Lecture 8 — Impact elasticities and leakage
item.description: Session 8 of Sustainable finance PhD course. Why secondary-market decarbonisation usually changes the portfolio before the world, and where impact claims can survive a counterfactual. The recording is not a substitute for reading the papers.
item.itunes:subtitle: Broccardo–Hart–Zingales exit versus voice; Berk–van Binsbergen listed-market arithmetic; Edmans–Levit–Schneemeier socially responsible divestment. Pomorski.
item.itunes:title: Lecture 8 — Impact elasticities and leakage

item.title: Lecture 7 — Building your own climate data
item.description: Session 7 of Sustainable finance PhD course. Point-in-time vintages, reported versus estimated emissions, and why restatements cannot enter a historical signal. The recording is not a substitute for reading the papers.
item.itunes:subtitle: Zhang (JF 2025) release-date discipline; Aswani–Raghunandan–Rajgopal estimated versus disclosed; Pomorski. A downloaded database is not 2016’s information set.
item.itunes:title: Lecture 7 — Building your own climate data

item.title: Lecture 6 — Can ESG even be measured?
item.description: Session 6 of Sustainable finance PhD course. Ratings disagreement, measurement error, and why aggregate ESG scores are a fragile object. The recording is not a substitute for reading the papers.
item.itunes:subtitle: Avramov ESG rating uncertainty; Berg ESG confusion and returns; Pomorski. A composite score is not one economic variable.
item.itunes:title: Lecture 6 — Can ESG even be measured?

item.title: Lecture 5 — The greenium
item.description: Session 5 of Sustainable finance PhD course. Preferences, expected versus realised green returns, institutional tilts, and flow-driven performance. D’Amico Bund-twin identification is not in this recording. The recording is not a substitute for reading the papers.
item.itunes:subtitle: Pástor–Stambaugh–Taylor equilibrium and review; Green Tilts; van der Beck flow-driven returns. Realised green performance is not expected return.
item.itunes:title: Lecture 5 — The greenium

item.title: Lecture 4 — Carbon, cash flows, and the look-ahead trap
item.description: Session 4 of Sustainable finance PhD course. Look-ahead in carbon returns (Zhang), estimated versus disclosed emissions (Aswani et al.), cash-flow versus discount-rate (Pomorski). Recording is not a substitute for reading the papers.
item.itunes:subtitle: Zhang (JF 2025), Aswani–Raghunandan–Rajgopal (RoF 2024), Pomorski ch. 3. Carbon premium versus investable information set.
item.itunes:title: Lecture 4 — Carbon, cash flows, and the look-ahead trap

item.title: Lecture 3 — Flows, not alpha
item.description: Seminar session on van der Beck Flow-Driven ESG Returns and Giglio et al. Four Facts. Not a substitute for reading the papers.
item.itunes:title: Lecture 3 — Flows, not alpha

item.title: Lecture 2 — ESG-integration and the ESG-efficient frontier
item.description: Seminar session on Pedersen–Fitzgibbons–Pomorski (ESG-efficient frontier) and Pastor–Stambaugh–Taylor Green Tilts. Not a substitute for reading the papers.
item.itunes:title: Lecture 2 — ESG-integration and the ESG-efficient frontier
